title: Aspect's experiments
reading: In 1972 Stuart Freedman and John Clauser in California measure polarisation correlations of pairs of light quanta from calcium atoms and find Bell's inequality violated. In 1982 Alain Aspect and his colleagues at Orsay, near Paris, repeat the experiment with far greater precision: in one arrangement they measure S = 2.697 ± 0.015 against a quantum prediction of 2.70 — violating the local bound of 2 by more than forty standard deviations. In another, the polariser settings are switched while the light quanta are in flight, so that no signal travelling at the speed of light could inform one side of the other's setting in time. The inequality is still violated.
detail: The 1982 switching was quasi-periodic rather than random, leaving a residual locality loophole, and detector efficiencies were low, requiring a fair-sampling assumption (the detection loophole). Both loopholes were closed simultaneously only in 2015.

claim.label: Detectors and switches
claim.summary: Speculative extrapolation: Einstein would press on the remaining assumptions — detection efficiency and the periodic switching — before surrendering separability.
voice: Impressive. But you tell me the counters catch only a small fraction of the pairs, and the switches follow a regular rhythm. I would want to see the same result with nearly every pair counted and the settings chosen by chance. Until then I will call it very strong evidence — not yet a verdict.
claim.reasoning: Loopholes remain; a principle should yield only to a clean experiment.

claim.label: Coincidence counting works
claim.summary: Inference: Compton's own 1925 work, like Bothe and Geiger's, used coincidences between individual events to settle a question of principle. He would recognise the method.
voice: This is our method, carried a long way. Bothe and Geiger counted coincidences to settle whether conservation held in single events; Simon and I did it with photographs. Here they count coincidences of pairs to settle whether distant results are independent. I trust the method. I would want to know the efficiencies, as any experimenter would.

claim.label: As expected
voice: The theory predicted the result and the result came. I would only warn against the language of influences travelling between the two sides. Nothing travels. There is one phenomenon, defined by the whole arrangement.

claim.label: Nonlocal, then
claim.summary: De Broglie lived until 1987; we have not found a documented reaction to Aspect. Inference from the logic of his theory.
voice: Then whatever determines the particles must connect them across the distance. My wave does that. I would rather accept a guiding wave that acts across space than give up the reality of the particle.

claim.label: How many pairs are lost?
claim.summary: Speculative; grounded only in experimental practice.
voice: I would ask the experimenters one thing before anything else: of every hundred pairs produced, how many are counted? A result that rests on a small fraction deserves care.
